newsitem.title: UK: UK TV watchdog says celebrity ad breached code.
newsitem.headline: UK TV watchdog says celebrity ad breached code.

text.p: Britain's television watchdog said on Monday the broadcast of an advertisement featuring presenter Anthea Turner following her appearance on a charity snooker programme violated regulatory codes.

Turner, a television celebrity and former news presenter, was shown in an advertisement for The Sun newspaper in a break during the Charity Snooker Challenger on Britain's ITV network in early January. A pre-recorded clip of Anthea interviewing key snooker players was shown in the Yorkshire region just before the Sun advert featuring Turner was aired.
The Independent Television Commission (ITC) said the advert breached its code on artist separation.

The ITC said an advert for Promise toothpaste, which carried an endorsement by the British Dental Health Foundation, breached codes prohibiting recommendations by medical professionals or professional bodies. Zee TV, the cable and satellite channel which broadcast the ad, withdrew it early in the ITC investigation.

The ITC said its own staff intervened over an advert for a pre-Christmas shopping trip to France that included references to a casino on the cruise boat. ITC regulations prohibit ads for casino gambling, even when an advert may be ostensibly for another purpose. The ad was shown on SIS, a satellite channel shown only in betting shops.
